entries.title: Length-resolved SAW continuation kernel
entries.statement: For a finite graph G with inherited positive edge weights, C_m(G;v) is the sum of product weights over simple paths of exactly m edges starting at v, with a free terminal vertex; C_0(G;v)=1 for a retained v. In a uniform n-step origin-started SAW law, a realized k-edge prefix eta has a suffix law on G_eta with exact remaining length n-k, where G_eta deletes earlier prefix vertices and retains its tip. Obstacle avoidance therefore uses C_(n-k)(G_eta minus A;tip)/C_(n-k)(G_eta;tip), multiplied by the prefix-avoidance indicator. An all-length partition sum defines a different conditional law.
assumptions: Finite graph containing all n-step origin walks

entries.title: Draft first-collar-entrance counting bound
entries.statement: DRAFT checked counting reduction; integration referee for the newest fixed-length packet is pending. For nested forbidden edge sets A subset B, every length-n path avoiding A but using B has a unique first B edge(v,w), after k edges. Its prefix avoids B and its suffix avoids A with length n-k-1. Consequently its total count is at most sum over k=0,...,n-1 and oriented(v,w) in B minus A of c_k^B(0,v)*C_(n-k-1)^A(w). Unit edge weights are assumed; include the first-edge weight for a weighted version. Dropping mutual prefix/suffix avoidance increases the count and supplies no scale-uniform collar decay.
assumptions: Unit weights for the displayed counts

entries.title: Unproved fixed-length SAW disk-collar estimate
entries.statement: UNPROVED INPUT for an explicitly chosen version of P0003. Take a uniform n-step origin-started honeycomb SAW and scale its trace by s_n=n^(-3/4). For a fixed closed disk A centered at z of radius r<|z| and its concentric radius(1+epsilon)r disk B_epsilon, let Delta_n(epsilon)=P(the scaled trace avoids A but intersects B_epsilon). The requested bound is limsup_(n to infinity)Delta_n(epsilon)<=C(z,r)*epsilon^alpha for some alpha>0, finite C(z,r), and all sufficiently small epsilon. The n limit comes first. This modulus is not proved by the finite continuation identity, a Doob inequality, or the first-entrance counting bound. Even proving it would still leave SLE identification, ordered-curve tightness, and the scale/continuum conventions open.
assumptions: epsilon small enough that the enlarged disk avoids the origin
